newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eight bids for 50pct stake in Duesseldorf airport.
newsitem.headline: Eight bids for 50pct stake in Duesseldorf airport.

text.p: Eight German and international firms or consortia have made bids to buy a 50 percent holding in Duesseldorf airport, a North Rhine Westphalia economics ministry spokesman said.
Eight out of 13 consortia which showed interest in purchasing the state's 50 percent airport stake during a pre-qualification stage made concrete offers by the June 4 deadline, he added.

North Rhine Westphalia decided to sell its stake in Duesseldorf, Germany's third-largest airport, because of the estimated two billion marks ($1.2 billion) needed for reconstruction and modernisation of the airport following last April's serious fire.
The other 50 percent stake in Duesseldorf airport is held by the city of Duesseldorf.

Purchase offers have been made by Frankfurt airport Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), German building company Hochtief and a consortium of German property firm Harpen AG and U.S. airports operator Airport Group International, sources close to the bidders said.
A consortium of Aeroports de Paris (ADP) and German property group IVG, BAA plc and Flughafen Wien were among foreign airport operators which made bids.
The other two offers came from Swiss-Swedish multinational ABB AG and a consortium of German construction firm Strabag Bau and state-owned Irish airport operator Aer Rianta.
Among the groups which withdrew from making an offer was Schiphol Airport, which saw Duesseldorf as playing a feeder service role into Amsterdam, industry observers said.
The offers will be narrowed down to two or three by the start of July with a final decision in favour of one company or consortium expected in September, they added.
